summary: The comparison is now complete and the condition reads consistently across every cell. Locally, a 100 ms tick period with a two-tick follower flush returned the correct index (returned 4, entry 33 at 4, decided values 11,12,22,33,34,35) and reported `decided_after_buffering` 2 — the origin's two deferred entries had already been flushed and decided before the partition instead of sitting in its batch across the re-synchronisation. Read together with the previous cells and the source, that replaces both the tick-period band and the flush-deadline rule with one condition: the shift needs the origin's deferred entries to still be in its batch when the re-synchronisation truncates them, and the flush and the truncation to fall inside one tick window. It fits all six configurations — the default flush deadline at 500 and 1000 ms ticks (deadline exceeds the run, entries still queued, shift), 100 and 250 ms ticks (deadline fires first, no shift), and a two-tick deadline at 1000 or 100 ms (entries flushed early, no shift). I corrected the knowledge entry's statement and conditions accordingly (revision 7), updated the discriminator to the one remaining unmeasured case (entries discarded while the origin's decided index also carries progress), and submitted the new case as a revision whose flush deadline is now a parameter, so the last cell has a receipt. Incomplete: that receipt is pending, and the remaining unmeasured case would show the mechanism's intermediate steps rather than only its endpoints.
